i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col i: destroyed — no preserved text. The opening of the Cycle is lost; from the surviving narrative arc (Smith 1994 vol 1, pp. 152-156) the lost opening probably set the scene of the divine assembly at the abode of ʾIlu (= El) on Mount Lel and announced Yammu's exaltation as challenger to Baʿlu.]

[KTU 1.1 col ii: top of column lost; preserved text begins mid-speech with what appears to be a divine summons-formula (the 'hasten your feet' speed-of-travel formula characteristic of divine messenger-speeches throughout the Cycle).]
[Hasten, urge, speed to] me, your feet —
[let them race to me, let] your legs [hasten];
[to the midst of the mountain GR(?)] is [your] message; and set —
[…] upon your shoulder(?).
[…] lapis-lazuli.
[…] he raises (his voice) in the midst (of).
[…] (those) days, two days.
[… his throat(?)], and [I will] go(?).
[… craft]smen set down to the earth.
[…] lips(?) set down.
[…] they pass by.
[…] return(?), your god.
[…] there is no entryway in the thousand-courts.
[At the f]eet of ʿAnatu
[he bows and falls down, he] prostrates himself, and he —
[honors her; he raises his voice and] cries — Message of —
[Bull ʾIlu, your father; word of the Be]nevolent One, your patriarch:

[KTU 1.2 col i: opening lines fragmentary. [KTU 1.2 col iv: top fragmentary; lower text is the most famous scene in the entire Cycle — the DUEL OF BAʿLU AND YAMMU. Kothar-wa-Khasis forges two magical mace-weapons named Yagrush ('Let-him-drive-out') and Ayamur ('Driver'); Baʿlu strikes Yammu twice; Yammu collapses; Baʿlu's kingship is proclaimed by ʿAṯtartu and the gods.]

i18n.en: His joints did not give way; his frame did not crumble.
Kothar arranged the two maces,
and proclaimed their (two) names:
Your name, you, is Ayamur ('Driver')!
Ayamur — drive Yammu away!

Naharu from the dais of his dominion!

Baʿlu drew (him in)(?), and he drained Yammu;

By name, ʿAṯtartu rebukes (him).

editorial_questions.issue: Divine name ʿAnatu (ʿnt) — Ugaritic warrior-goddess; first occurrence in this chapter. Hebrew Bible counterpart attested only obliquely (place-name Beth-Anath Josh 19:38; the figure ʿănat in Judg 3:31/5:6; Anat-Yahu at Elephantine). Render as 'ʿAnatu' (Ugaritic vocalization, project policy) vs. 'ʿAnat' (Hebrew/comparative form) vs. 'Anath' (older English convention).

Divine name ʾIlu (ʾil) — the head of the Ugaritic pantheon, Northwest-Semitic cognate of Hebrew ʾēl / ʾĕlōhîm. Major cross-corpus parallel to Hebrew Bible El/Elohim. Standard epithets attested in this chapter: ṯr ʾil ('Bull ʾIlu'), lṭpn ('Benevolent One'), d pʾid ('kind-hearted'), ʾab šnm ('Father of Years'), ḥtk ('patriarch'). Production glossary has entry id 'elohim-as-translation' (wohChoice 'the Elohim') scoped to Hebrew Bible refIds, not Ugaritic. Render Ugaritic ʾil as 'ʾIlu' (project policy: Ugaritic vocalization) vs. 'El' vs. 'God' vs. 'the Elohim' (extending Hebrew entry cross-corpus).

Standing epithet ṯr ʾil ('Bull ʾIlu' / 'Bull-El'). Cross-corpus to Hebrew 'Mighty One/Bull of Jacob' (ʾăbîr Yaʿăqōb, Gen 49:24, Ps 132:2,5) and 'Bull of Israel' (ʾăbîr Yiśrāʾēl, Isa 1:24) — the theriomorphic patriarch-as-bull substrate. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads ʾabh as 'his father' in adjacent occurrences. Render 'Bull ʾIlu' vs. 'Bull El' vs. 'the Bull, ʾIlu' vs. expand epithet ('Bull-El, father of the gods').
options: the Mighty Bull (drop divine name, retain epithet)

editorial_questions.issue: The pacification-oracle qryy b ʾarṣ mlḥmt / rm ddym sk šlm / ʾarbdd l kbd šdm ('place war in the earth, pour peace into the midst, drop tranquility into the fields'). Reading of ddym contested: 'love-tokens' (Pardee 2003), 'mandrakes' (Gibson 1978), or 'mounds, hills' (Ginsberg 1955); cf. Hebrew dûdāʾîm 'mandrakes' Gen 30:14. Possible cross-corpus parallel with Isa 2:4 / Mic 4:3 'beat swords into plowshares' peace-oracle. Default renders ddym as 'love-tokens'.

Divine name Kothar-wa-Khasis (kṯr w ḫss, 'Skillful-and-Clever'), Ugaritic divine craftsman; alternate name Hayin (hyn). No exact Hebrew-Bible counterpart, though comparative parallels are drawn with Beṣalʾel (Exod 31:2-5) and with the divine-craftsman type cross-traditions (Hephaistos / Enki-Nudimmud / Ptah). Render as binomial 'Kothar-wa-Khasis' vs. translate epithet 'Skillful-and-Clever' vs. anglicize 'Kothar' alone.

The famous mystery-revelation formula rgm ʿṣ wlḫšt ʾabn ('a word of tree, a whisper of stone'). Default renders literally. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads as a fixed liturgical pair denoting esoteric cosmic communication; older readings (Ginsberg 1955) gloss 'message of timber and stone' (architectural). Possible cross-corpus parallel with Hab 2:11 ('the stone shall cry out from the wall, and the beam from the timber shall answer it'); Ps 19:1-4 (heavens' speech).
options: word of tree and whisper of stone (literal, default)
message of wood and stone (architectural reading, Ginsberg)
editorial_questions.default_taken: word of tree and whisper of stone

editorial_questions.issue: tʾunt šmm ʿm ʾarṣ thmt ʿmn kbkbm — 'converse of heaven with earth, of the deeps with the stars'. Major cross-corpus candidate with Ps 19:1-4 (heavens declare the glory of God); Hebrew thwm 'deep' and Ugaritic thmt are cognate (cf. Gen 1:2). Render tʾunt as 'converse' vs. 'communication' vs. 'intercourse' vs. 'speech'.

ʿnn ʾilm — 'cloud-attendants of the gods' (a class of divine messenger/servant). The word ʿnn (lit. 'cloud') marks them as cloud-traveling envoys, cognate to the Hebrew root ʿnn 'cloud'. Render 'attendants of the gods' (default, dropping cloud-imagery) vs. 'cloud-attendants of the gods' (literal) vs. 'servants of the gods' vs. 'divine messengers'. Lens-risk: 'cloud-attendants' could echo Baʿlu's later 'Rider of the Clouds' epithet and the NT 'coming on clouds' motif — flag for Editor.

ḏd ʾil — 'pavilion / abode of ʾIlu'; qrš mlk — 'dwelling-tent of the King'. qrš is cognate to Hebrew qereš ('plank' of the tabernacle, Exod 26). Strong cross-corpus to the Mosaic tabernacle vocabulary. Render qrš as 'dwelling-tent' (default) vs. 'tabernacle' (Bible-resonant) vs. 'plank-shrine' (literal-architectural).

ʾab šnm — 'Father of Years' (epithet of ʾIlu). MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS candidate with Daniel 7:9 ʿattîq yômîn ('Ancient of Days'); both are paternal-eternity epithets of the head-of-pantheon. Render 'Father of Years' (literal, default) vs. 'the Ancient One' vs. 'Ancient of Days' (Bible-resonant).

Bull-of-pantheon epithet recurs (ṯr ʾil ʾabh, 'Bull ʾIlu his father'). The theriomorphic bull-El imagery is the substrate the Hebrew Bible polemicizes against (cf. golden calf, Exod 32; Jeroboam's bull-shrines, 1 Kgs 12). See also ed.q. on BCY-WOH-1.1-ii:18.
options: the Mighty Bull, his father (drop name)

editorial_questions.issue: mrzḥ — the marzeaḥ ritual-banquet. MANDATORY cross-corpus parallel with Hebrew Bible marzēaḥ (Amos 6:7 'feast of the sprawlers' / bêt marzēaḥ; Jer 16:5 'house of mourning-feast'). The Ugaritic marzeaḥ is one of the most-discussed ANE banqueting institutions. Render 'marzeaḥ-feast' (transliterate, default) vs. 'drinking-banquet' (translate) vs. 'feast' (generic).

**THE YW LINE — MANDATORY MAJOR**: šm bny yw ʾilt — 'The name of my son is YW, O goddess'. THE PROTO-YHWH CANDIDATE. Three named-scholarship readings: (a) de Moor 1971 reads YW as a divine name independent of YHWH but phonologically similar; (b) Cross 1973 (CMHE) treats YW as 'probably YHWH-related, a short form of Yahweh attested in the West-Semitic divine onomastics'; (c) Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 151-160 is cautiously open — notes the Y-W consonants match the Yahwistic short theophoric ending (-yw, -yāhû) but argues the line gives YW to *Yammu* (the Sea-god, antagonist), which complicates any straight equation with YHWH. Massive lens-risk. Default renders as bare transliteration 'YW' with no glossing.
options: Yaw (vocalized — but commits to a vocalization)
Yammu (renames the deity to make the equation 'YW = Yammu' explicit)

editorial_questions.issue: ʾilt — 'goddess' (vocative). Refers most plausibly to ʾAṯiratu (= Asherah, ʾIlu's consort). Render 'goddess' (default, generic) vs. 'ʾIlatu' (name-form, reading ʾilt as a proper name for ʾIlu's female counterpart) vs. 'O ʾAṯiratu' (identify the goddess explicitly).

mdd ʾil ('Beloved of ʾIlu'), standard epithet of Yammu in this chapter. Compare Hebrew Bible yĕdîd ('beloved') applied to Israel/Benjamin (Deut 33:12) and to Solomon (Yedidyah, 2 Sam 12:25). Render 'Beloved of ʾIlu' (default) vs. 'Darling of ʾIlu' vs. 'ʾIlu's Beloved'.

ʾaliyn bʿl ('Mighty Baʿlu' / 'Mightiest Baʿlu' / 'Victor Baʿlu'). Standard epithet recurring throughout the Cycle. Render 'Mighty Baʿlu' (default) vs. 'Mightiest Baʿlu' (superlative) vs. 'Victor Baʿlu' vs. 'Baʿlu the Powerful'.

Kingship-deposition formula gršnn l ksʾi mlkh l nḫt l kḥṯ drkth ('drive him out from the throne of his kingship, from the seat, from the dais of his dominion'). MAJOR cross-corpus parallel with Isa 14:13 (Helal ben Shahar's deposition); Ezek 28 (Tyre); Ps 89:5. The throne-deposition vocabulary is shared NW-Semitic kingship-ideology. The verb grš ('drive out') is also the verb of the Eden expulsion Gen 3:24 — flag for Editor.

Mount Ṣapunu (b ṣpn) — Baʿlu's holy mountain (modern Jebel al-Aqra in Syria). MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew ṣāpôn ('north') and Ps 48:3 yarketê ṣāpôn ('recesses of the north') applied to Mount Zion. Render 'Ṣapunu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Zaphon' (Hebrew-conventional) vs. 'Mount Ṣapunu' (with title) vs. 'the North' (translate).

Haddu (hd) — the personal name of the storm-deity whose cult-title is Baʿlu ('Lord'). Cross-corpus with Hebrew Bible Hadad (1 Kgs 11:14) and with Akkadian Adad. Default renders as 'Haddu' (Ugaritic vocalization).

mbkm — 'springs / sources (of the deep)'. Cross-corpus with Hebrew nibkê tĕhôm (Job 38:16, 'the springs of the deep'). Both reflect a shared NW-Semitic cosmography of abyssal water-sources at the base of the cosmos. Render 'springs (of the deep)' (default, with gloss) vs. 'springs of the abyss' vs. 'sources of the deep'.

Divine name Yammu (ym) — the Sea-god, Baʿlu's antagonist in this chapter. MAJOR cross-corpus: Hebrew yām ('sea'); the Chaoskampf-with-the-sea pattern of Ps 74:13-14, Ps 89:10-11, Isa 27:1, Hab 3:8, Ps 18:16 (rebuke of waters); Job 26:12. Render 'Yammu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Yam' (Hebrew-conventional / comparative form) vs. 'Sea' (translate).

mlʾak — 'messenger, envoy'. The lemma is the etymological source of Hebrew malʾāk (also 'angel') and ultimately Greek angelos. Render 'messenger' (default, neutral) vs. 'envoy' vs. 'angel' (committing to the Bible-resonant gloss).

ṯpṭ nhr — 'Judge River / Judge Naharu'. Yammu's binomial partner-name in standing parallelism Yammu // Naharu. nhr = 'river' (cognate to Hebrew nāhār). Render 'Judge Naharu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Judge River' (translate nhr) vs. 'Judge Nahar' vs. 'Ruler River' (translate ṯpṭ too). The parallel Yam/Nahar (Sea/River) is itself a major comparative-mythology marker (cf. Ps 24:2, 89:25-26).

Divine name Daganu (dgn) — Baʿlu's father (bn dgn 'son of Daganu'). MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew Dāgôn (Judg 16:23; 1 Sam 5:2-7); the Philistine grain-deity. Render 'Daganu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Dagan' (Akkadian-conventional) vs. 'Dagon' (Hebrew Bible form).

pḏ — 'gold' (the booty Yammu demands of Baʿlu). The exact sense ('gold' vs. 'wealth' vs. 'redemption-payment') is debated. Hebrew pdh = 'to redeem', and the Ugaritic noun pḏh has been read both as 'gold/wealth' (Gibson 1978) and as 'ransom' (Pardee 2003 cautious). Default renders 'gold'.

pḫr mʿd — 'gathered assembly' (the divine council). MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew Bible bĕnê hāʾĕlōhîm convening (Job 1:6; 2:1; Ps 82:1; Ps 89:6-8 sôd qĕdōšîm); cf. Akkadian puḫru ša ilāni. The bn qdš ('holy sons') at 1.2-i:21 also belongs here. Render 'gathered assembly' (default) vs. 'divine council' (Bible-resonant) vs. 'assembly of the gods'.

bn qdš — 'holy sons' (= the divine council members). MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew bĕnê (hā)ʾĕlōhîm (Gen 6:2,4; Job 1:6; 2:1; 38:7; Ps 29:1, 89:7; Deut 32:8 LXX) and bĕnê ʿelyôn (Ps 82:6). The 'sons of god' divine-assembly is shared NW-Semitic theology. Render 'holy sons' (default, literal) vs. 'sons of the Holy One' vs. 'sons of god' (Bible-resonant).

Heads-onto-knees gesture (tġly ʾilm rʾišthm l ẓr brkthm). The gods' physical posture of fear before Yammu's envoys. Cross-corpus to Elijah's posture at Carmel (1 Kgs 18:42, head between knees) and to lamentation postures. Default renders descriptively without commitment to a specific cross-corpus echo.
options: lowered their heads onto the tops of their knees (literal, default)
bowed their heads to their knees
put their heads between their knees (Elijah-resonant)
editorial_questions.default_taken: lowered their heads onto the tops of their knees

editorial_questions.issue: ygʿr — 'rebukes' (Baʿlu rebuking the cowering gods). MAJOR cross-corpus vocabulary: the gāʿar pattern of YHWH's rebuke of the sea / chaos-waters (Ps 18:15-16, 104:7, Isa 17:13, Nah 1:4). This verb is one of the central Chaoskampf-rebuke lexemes shared across NW-Semitic. Default renders 'rebukes'.

ʾišt ʾištm yʾitmr ḥrb lṭšt b lšnhm — 'a fire, two fires they kindle; a sharpened sword on their tongues'. MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew Bible tongue-as-sword imagery (Ps 57:5 'their tongues are sharp swords'; Ps 64:4; Prov 12:18; cf. Heb 4:12 'sharper than a two-edged sword'; James 3:6 'the tongue is a fire'). The fire/sword-tongue is shared NW-Semitic hostile-speech topos. Default renders literally.
options: a fire, two fires they kindle — a sharpened sword on their tongues (literal, default)
their tongues blazed like fire, sharp as swords (paraphrase)
fire flashed in their mouths, sword-edged on their tongues
editorial_questions.default_taken: a fire, two fires they kindle — a sharpened sword on their tongues (literal)

editorial_questions.issue: **THE CONCESSION**: ʿbdk bʿl y ymm ʿbdk bʿl — 'Your servant is Baʿlu, O Yammu! Your servant is Baʿlu.' ʾIlu submissively concedes Baʿlu to Yammu. The political crisis of the Cycle. Render 'your servant' (literal, default) vs. 'your slave' (stronger) vs. 'subject to you' (paraphrastic).

zbl bʿl — 'Prince Baʿlu' standing epithet (also zbl ym 'Prince Yammu', zbl bʿl ʾarṣ 'Prince Baʿlu of the Earth'). zbl cognate to Hebrew zĕbûl 'lofty habitation' (1 Kgs 8:13; Hab 3:11; Ps 49:14) and to the name Zebulun. Render 'Prince Baʿlu' (default) vs. 'Lord Baʿlu' vs. 'the Exalted Baʿlu'.

ʾaṣṭ and mʿsṣṣt — both apparently weapons or weapon-types Baʿlu grasps in his rage. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads these as 'striking-weapon' and 'smiting-weapon' respectively but acknowledges both are obscure. Pardee 2003 leaves the line largely untranslated. Default renders descriptively as 'striking-(weapon)' and 'smiting-(weapon)' with explicit uncertainty.

Divine name ʿAṯtartu (ʿṯtrt) — warrior-goddess; here paired with ʿAnatu in restraining Baʿlu. MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew ʿAštōret (1 Kgs 11:5; Judg 2:13), Greek Astarte, Phoenician ʿštrt. The double-goddess restraint scene is one of the few preserved instances of ʿAnatu-ʿAṯtartu paired action. Render 'ʿAṯtartu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Astarte' (Greek-conventional / comparative) vs. 'Ashtart'.

mġnt — uncertain reading. Either D-yqtl 2ms of mġn 'to strike, smite' (giving 'How can you strike the messengers?') or a noun mġnt 'gift, present' related to mgn 'shield' (giving 'How is the gift / shield / present of the messengers?'). Smith 1994 vol 1 prefers the strike-reading; Pardee 2003 raises the alternative. Default takes the strike-reading.

Ḥôrânu (ḥrn) — minor Ugaritic divinity invoked in curse-formulae. Cross-corpus with the divine name Ḥōrān attested at Beth-Ḥôrôn in Hebrew Bible (place-name). Reading ambiguous: ḥrn could be the deity Ḥôrânu (Smith 1994) or 'a noble/scorching curse' (Gibson 1978). Default takes Ḥôrânu as deity with parenthetical query.

qdqd — 'crown of the head, scalp'. MANDATORY cross-corpus with Hebrew qodqōd (Ps 68:22 'God will smite the head/qodqōd of his enemies'; Deut 33:20; Hab 3:13; Jer 2:16). The head-smiting (mḫṣ qdqd) is a central Chaoskampf motif extending to YHWH's defeat of his enemies. Default renders 'crown'.

**ʾAṯiratu**: ʾaṯrt — the Ugaritic mother-goddess, ʾIlu's consort, mother of the gods (bnh 'her sons' = the divine assembly). MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew Bible Asherah (1 Kgs 18:19 '450 prophets of Asherah'; Deut 16:21; Jer 17:2; the asherah-poles polemic). The full title rbt ʾaṯrt ym 'Lady ʾAṯiratu of the Sea' is attested elsewhere in the Cycle. ʾilt 'goddess' = her title. Render 'ʾAṯiratu' (Ugaritic vocalization, default) vs. 'Asherah' (Bible-conventional) vs. 'Athirat'.

zbl bʿl ʾarṣ — 'Prince Baʿlu of the Earth' / 'Prince Baʿlu of the Underworld'. ʾarṣ here is contested: 'earth' (default) or 'underworld/netherworld' (Smith 1994 vol 1 — the netherworld-king reading, which prefigures the Môtu cycle). Default renders 'of the Earth' but flags.

**MAJOR — rkb ʿrpt** ('Rider of the Clouds'), THE central epithet of Baʿlu, recurring at 1.2 IV 8, 29; 1.3 II 40; 1.3 IV 4; 1.4 III 11, V 7, etc. MANDATORY cross-corpus parallel: Hebrew rōkēb bā-ʿărābôt (Ps 68:5, often rendered 'rider on the clouds' / 'rider on the deserts' depending on textual decision); Deut 33:26; Ps 18:11 (YHWH-on-cherub-rides). The NT Christological appropriation (Matt 26:64; Mark 14:62; Rev 1:7 'coming on the clouds'; Dan 7:13 'one like a son of man with the clouds of heaven') extends the motif. Render 'Rider of the Clouds' (default) vs. 'Cloud-Rider' vs. 'Rider on the Clouds' vs. (lens-risky) avoid Christological-resonant 'Cloud-Coming One'.

mlk ʿlm ('eternal kingship') — MAJOR cross-corpus with Hebrew malkût ʿōlām (Ps 145:13 'thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom'); melek ʿôlām (Jer 10:10 'the LORD is the true God…an everlasting King'); the eternal-king Davidic-promise (2 Sam 7:13, 16). The eternal-kingship epithet is shared NW-Semitic royal theology. Default renders 'eternal kingship'.
dt drdrk — 'of generation upon generation'. Cross-corpus with Hebrew dōr wādôr / lədōr wādōr (Ps 89:2, 4; Lam 5:19). Default renders literally 'generation upon generation'.

**WEAPON NAME — Yagrush** (ygrš), the first mace, 'Let-him-drive-out'. Name from G-yqtl of grš 'to drive out, expel'. MAJOR cross-corpus: cognate to Hebrew gāraš (the verb of expulsion from Eden, Gen 3:24 'he drove out the man'; cf. also Sarah's casting-out of Hagar, Gen 21:10). Default renders the weapon-name as transliteration plus parenthetical gloss 'Yagrush (Let-him-drive-out)'.

grš ym l ksʾih — 'drive Yammu from his throne'. Cf. Isa 14:13 deposition-from-throne; Ps 89:5; Ezek 28. Throne-deposition vocabulary shared NW-Semitic kingship-ideology. See also editorial question on BCY-WOH-1.1-iv:24.

**WEAPON NAME — Ayamur** (ʾaymr), the second mace. Etymology debated: (a) from mwr 'to drive away/cast out' (Smith 1994 vol 1: 'May-he-drive-away' or 'Driver'); (b) from ʾamr 'to expel' (Pardee 2003: 'Expeller'); (c) Gibson 1978 'All-Driver' (intensive). Default renders 'Ayamur (Driver)'.

**MAJOR — the head-smiting motif**: hlm qdqd zbl ym — 'strike the crown of Prince Yammu'; in v.35 the parallel 'between the eyes of Judge Naharu'. MANDATORY cross-corpus with Ps 68:22 ('God will smite the head/qodqōd of his enemies, the hairy crown of him who walks in his guilty ways'); Hab 3:13 'you smashed the head from the house of the wicked'; Deut 33:20; Num 24:17 (Balaam 'shall smite the corners/qodqōd of Moab'). The head-smiting + between-the-eyes pattern is the central Chaoskampf victory-image of NW-Semitic mythology, extending to YHWH-vs-Leviathan (Ps 74:13-14) and to Jael-vs-Sisera (Judg 5:26). Default renders literally.
options: strike the crown … between the eyes (default, literal)
smash the head … between the eyes (stronger verb)
smite the crown … between the eyes (Bible-resonant)
editorial_questions.default_taken: strike the crown … between the eyes

editorial_questions.issue: yqṯ bʿl w yšt ym — the famous crux of the duel's resolution. yqṯ uncertain: 'gathers up / draws together' (Smith 1994 vol 1: 'Baʿlu drags Yam'), 'destroys' (some older readings), or 'cuts off' (Pardee 2003 tentative). yšt = G-yqtl of šty 'to drink' (cognate Hebrew šātâ), which gives 'and he drank Yammu' — a dismemberment/devouring image — OR yšt could be reread as 'to set, place' (homograph). The wordplay šty 'drink' on ym (also = 'day', possibly 'sea-drinkable'); cf. the Marduk-Tiamat scattering at Enuma Eliš IV. Default renders 'Baʿlu drew (him in)(?), and he drained Yammu' with the (him in)/drink-ambiguity preserved.
options: Baʿlu drew (him in), and drained Yammu (Smith 1994, default)
Baʿlu cut down, and dismembered Yammu (stronger)
Baʿlu seized, and drank up Yammu (literal drink-reading)
Baʿlu drew his weapon, and set Yammu (alt. yšt reading)
editorial_questions.default_taken: Baʿlu drew (him in)(?), and drained Yammu

editorial_questions.issue: b šm tgʿrm ʿṯtrt — closing line of the duel. 'By name, ʿAṯtartu rebukes (him).' tgʿrm picks up the same gʿr ('rebuke') verb used by Baʿlu against the gods at 1.2-i:25, which is also the Hebrew gāʿar of YHWH's rebuke of the sea (Ps 18:15; 104:7; Isa 17:13; Nah 1:4). ʿAṯtartu's rebuke seals the victory and parallels the YHWH-rebukes-sea pattern. Reading of b šm is contested: 'by name' (incantation-reading), 'with shame' (Pardee 2003 alternative reading b šm as 'shame'), 'as for the name' (Smith 1994). Default renders 'By name'.
options: As for the name, ʿAṯtartu rebukes (Smith 1994)
In the name (of Baʿlu), ʿAṯtartu rebukes

editorial_questions.issue: Lacuna restoration of the standard hasten-formula opening. The triplet ḥwš // ʿṣ // ʿbṣ ('hasten, urge, speed') is well-attested elsewhere in the Cycle, so the restoration is high-confidence. Default follows the standard restoration. Flag for Editor whether the project should mark such formulaic restorations differently (e.g. as confident vs. speculative).
options: Follow standard formulaic restoration (default, current practice)
Render as ambiguous '[…]' with no commitment
Mark restoration with confidence-level tag in commentary

editorial_questions.issue: ʾiwrkl — obscure name/epithet. No fixed reading; Smith 1994 vol 1 leaves untranslated; older editions sometimes proposed 'O Lord(?)' or treated as a deity. Default keeps as transliteration with parenthetical query.
The opening line is so damaged that multiple sign-readings are possible per Smith 1994 vol 1. Source notes preserve '/' multireading markers. Default renders as '[…] (signs uncertain) […]'.
options: attempt restoration based on parallel-passage formulas

editorial_questions.issue: mll — uncertain: 'utterance, word' (cf. Hebrew mll 'speak') or 'pulverization' (cf. Aramaic mll II 'crush'). Default takes the speech-reading 'like utterances(?)' with explicit uncertainty.

bṯt — multiple readings: 'shame, confusion' (Smith 1994 vol 1 tentative); btt 'wine-skin' (older readings); 'song-line' (a few scholars). ʿllmn 'youths/lads/attendants' is reasonably secure. Default renders 'confusion(?)' with explicit uncertainty.

ʾalp ḥẓr — 'thousand-courts' (numerical pair-formula). Some readings render 'a thousand (entries) at a courtyard'; others as a generic numerical-amplification idiom. Default renders 'thousand-courts'.
